prerequisites.title: Paid SurveyMonkey plan
prerequisites.detail: Creating and deploying an OAuth app requires a paid plan. Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register a draft app.

prerequisites.title: Not a SurveyMonkey competitor
prerequisites.detail: Competitors may not open a Developer Account.

prerequisites.title: Your own OAuth app for Composio
prerequisites.detail: Composio has no managed app for SurveyMonkey, so you need your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Register an app in Developer Portal
steps.detail: Sign in with a paid SurveyMonkey account and use Add a New App. Choose Private or Public as the scenario requires.
steps.done_when: A draft app exists in My Apps.

steps.title: Prepare scopes and redirect URL
steps.detail: Choose the minimum scopes and mark essential ones Required. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and enter it on the Settings tab.
steps.done_when: Scopes and redirect URL saved on Settings.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the survey_monkey auth config with your client ID and secret from the app's Overview tab.

steps.title: Draft the app listing
steps.detail: Write an honest English listing covering core functionality and scope requirements. Avoid generic names, versioning, and the word SurveyMonkey.

steps.title: Submit listing for approval
steps.detail: Create the listing in the listings tab and submit it. Confirm support, HTTPS and pricing statements.

steps.title: Wait for SurveyMonkey approval
steps.done_when: App approved for the App Directory.

steps.title: Deploy before the 90-day window ends
steps.detail: Click Deploy in the top right of the app page.
steps.done_when: App is deployed as Private or Public.

traps.title: Published Public apps in the App Directory can make
traps.detail: Published Public apps in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

traps.title: Draft and Private apps are rate-limited, and the limit
traps.detail: Draft and Private apps are rate-limited, and the limit resets daily at 12:00 AM GMT; three violations of up to 150% are tolerated in a 30-day window before enforcement at 100% begins.

traps.title: Enforcement at 100% begins once an app exceeds its
traps.detail: Enforcement at 100% begins once an app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.

traps.title: Draft app expires after 90 days
traps.detail: If you don't deploy within 90 days, the app is disabled. You must then deploy or ask the help center for an extension.

traps.title: Private app blocks outside customers
traps.detail: All users must be on the same team, and other accounts cannot authenticate a draft app.

traps.title: Customers may need paid plans
traps.detail: Customers lacking the plan for paid scopes are asked to upgrade, and OAuth fails if required scopes are unavailable.

blockers.symptom: Create/Modify scopes rejected in a Public app
blockers.what_it_means: These two scopes need separate SurveyMonkey approval.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact the SurveyMonkey help center with your use case.

evidence.question: G11

evidence.question: G11

evidence.question: G11

evidence.question: G11

evidence.answer: Without SurveyMonkey's written authorization for a specific use case, the developer may not use the API or permit any Third-Party Client to access, process, transmit, or store certain restricted data.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.

evidence.quote: You do not need to register your own OAuth app.

evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: managed apps are the default when they are available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: with a managed app, end users see a Composio consent screen rather than the developer's app name during OAuth.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Fine for internal tools, prototypes, and development.
evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: managed apps are described as fine for internal tools, prototypes, and development, while production usually calls for the developer's own app name on consent screens.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio."
evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: in production, users should see the developer's app name rather than Composio on OAuth consent screens.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps (general, not SurveyMonkey-specific): managed apps share quota across all Composio users.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps (general, not SurveyMonkey-specific): a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Limit of managed apps (general, not SurveyMonkey-specific): managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: self-hosted or regional variants (for example a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: General statement, not specific to SurveyMonkey: a developer can mix approaches, using their own credentials for some toolkits and managed auth for others, with each toolkit having its own auth config.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: To proxy the OAuth redirect through your own domain, set the authorized redirect URI in your OAuth app's settings to your own endpoint (the page's example is on yourdomain.com).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The page's example redirect URI on your own domain is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect (an HTTPS URL).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token. Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through backend.composio.dev so Composio can capture the auth token, and some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: Proxying through your own domain is optional and is for when you need to hide Composio's domain.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: composio_url = "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback"
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint forwards the callback to Composio's callback URL on backend.composio.dev, the URL it hard-codes.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.
evidence.answer: Your proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect, not follow the redirect server-side or fetch Composio.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: The page is generic and does not mention SurveyMonkey; by default the provider consent screen shows Composio branding (e.g., on Google, GitHub, etc.).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own OAuth app
evidence.answer: The page's stated fix for Composio branding on the consent screen is to use your own OAuth app (generic guidance, not specific to SurveyMonkey).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: The page advises adding your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand (generic guidance, not specific to SurveyMonkey).

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app.
evidence.answer: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app (no separate developer program or plan is named for registering).

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Registering creates a draft app with an access token you can use to query against your account for 90 days.
evidence.answer: Registering creates a draft app with an access token usable against the developer's own account for 90 days.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Private apps don’t need to be reviewed by SurveyMonkey.
evidence.answer: Private apps do not need to be reviewed by SurveyMonkey.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey, and must adhere to its terms of use, before they can be published in the App Directory (applies to every Public app before listing).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account and published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account once published in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: For Public apps, the Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys scopes require SurveyMonkey's approval to use (only these two scopes are named as needing approval).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If you’ve deployed a Public app and want to change your scope requirements to include these, you’ll need to contact us at our help center to tell us more about your app and use case.
evidence.answer: A deployed Public app that wants to add those approval-required scopes must contact SurveyMonkey's help center and explain the app and use case.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access .
evidence.answer: A Private app's users must all belong to the same SurveyMonkey team, so it cannot be used by outside organizations.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: No other SurveyMonkey accounts can authenticate a draft app.
evidence.answer: Without a provider review, a draft app cannot be authenticated by any other SurveyMonkey account.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If your app will access many SurveyMonkey accounts, implement the OAuth 2.0 three-step flow outlined below to allow users to authorize your app to access their accounts.
evidence.answer: An app that will access many SurveyMonkey accounts must use the OAuth 2.0 three-step flow so each account's user authorizes the app.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If you have a Private app and will only access your own SurveyMonkey account, you can use the access token, generated when you registered your app, as part of your app’s configuration.
evidence.answer: A Private app used only for the developer's own account can use the access token generated at registration, with no OAuth flow.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Public apps use scopes to request permissions from app users during OAuth.
evidence.answer: Public apps request permissions (scopes) from app users during OAuth.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid plan (the page does not list which scopes a typical AI agent needs).

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid SurveyMonkey plan to create any collector that is not a weblink collector.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid plan for any collector that is not a weblink collector.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Two scopes (Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys) need SurveyMonkey approval in a Public app.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Basic plan accounts can access response details for up to 25 responses per survey.
evidence.answer: Basic plan accounts can access response details (responses_read_detail scope) for up to 25 responses per survey; paid plans have unlimited access.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: You can set scopes to be required, optional, or not required in your app’s settings .
evidence.answer: Each scope can be set in the app's settings as required, optional, or not required.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Our request headers include the scopes available to users’ plan, as well as those they’ve granted your app permission to.
evidence.answer: Request headers report the scopes available to the user's plan and the scopes the user has granted the app.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: All Draft and Private apps will initially be subject to request limits of 120 calls/minute and starting at 500 calls/day ( contact sales ).
evidence.answer: Draft and Private apps start with request limits of 120 calls per minute and 500 calls per day (the daily figure is described as a starting level, with sales contact mentioned).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: When a Public app is in draft (during development), it’s subject to draft request limits .
evidence.answer: A draft Public app is subject to draft request limits while it is in development.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Before the 90-day draft period ends, you must deploy your app or it’ll be disabled.
evidence.answer: Draft apps have a 90-day window; the app is disabled if it is not deployed before that period ends.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: If your app is disabled, you must deploy it or contact us at our help center to request an extension.
evidence.answer: A disabled app can be re-enabled only by deploying it or asking SurveyMonkey's help center for an extension.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Before the 90-day period ends, you must deploy your app as either Public or Private and upgrade your account as needed.
evidence.answer: Before the 90-day period ends, the developer must deploy the app as Public or Private and upgrade the account as needed.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Public apps published in our App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day to our API.
evidence.answer: Published Public apps in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: We permit three violations of up to 150% within a 30-day window.
evidence.answer: Draft and Private apps are rate-limited, and the limit resets daily at 12:00 AM GMT; three violations of up to 150% are tolerated in a 30-day window before enforcement at 100% begins.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: We begin to enforce limits at 100% once your app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.
evidence.answer: Enforcement at 100% begins once an app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Private apps have API request limits and higher limits are available for purchase .
evidence.answer: Private apps have API request limits, and higher limits can be purchased.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: In addition, requests made to the API to create contacts or send invite messages are subject to our sending and contact limits .
evidence.answer: Requests to create contacts or send invite messages are also subject to sending and contact limits.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Our access tokens don’t currently expire but may in the future.
evidence.answer: Access tokens do not currently expire, but may in the future; the page does not say tokens expire sooner in testing mode.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey will review all requests within 5 business days.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey reviews rate-limit increase requests within 5 business days (this is not an app-review timeline; the page gives no app review timeline).

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan, so the customer, not only the developer, may need to pay.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: If your Public app uses scopes tied to paid plans, any accounts attempting to authenticate without the necessary plan will be asked to upgrade to proceed.
evidence.answer: If a Public app uses paid-plan scopes, accounts without the required plan are asked to upgrade before they can proceed.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Private apps have API request limits and higher limits are available for purchase .
evidence.answer: Higher API request limits for Private apps can be bought.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.
evidence.answer: Increased rate limits may incur additional fees.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access .
evidence.answer: Private app users must have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Basic plans can retrieve up to 25 responses per survey
evidence.answer: Basic plans can retrieve up to 25 responses per survey through the response-details scope; paid plans have unlimited response access.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Upgrade to a paid SurveyMonkey plan for unlimited response access
evidence.answer: Upgrading to a paid plan gives unlimited response access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your Public app uses scopes tied to paid plans, any accounts attempting to authenticate without the necessary plan will be asked to upgrade to proceed.
evidence.answer: Customers whose accounts lack the plan required by the app's paid-plan scopes are asked to upgrade before authenticating.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your app has required scopes , users will need to approve all of them and may need a paid SurveyMonkey plan to successfully OAuth into your app.
evidence.answer: Users must approve all required scopes, and may need a paid plan, to OAuth into the app.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: All required scopes must be approved by and available to the user for the OAuth process to succeed.
evidence.answer: All required scopes must be approved by and available to the user for OAuth to succeed.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The page presented to the user will identify your app, ask them to log into SurveyMonkey if they aren’t already, and ask them to authorize any required scopes .
evidence.answer: The authorization page identifies the app and asks the user to log in and authorize required scopes; the page does not mention an admin approval step.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Your app will need to obtain additional access tokens for each SurveyMonkey account you wish to access.
evidence.answer: Each SurveyMonkey account the app wishes to access needs its own access token obtained through authorization.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Access tokens can be revoked by the user.
evidence.answer: The account owner can revoke an access token, after which the app must complete OAuth again.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri URL encoded OAuth redirect URI you registered for your app (can be found and edited here )
evidence.answer: The redirect URI must be one registered for the app, and can be found and edited in the app settings.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey will generate a 302 redirect sending their browser to your redirect URI along with a short-lived code included as a query parameter (as well as the state parameter if it was specified originally).
evidence.answer: After authorization, SurveyMonkey redirects the browser to the app's redirect URI with a short-lived code.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your app needs to use that code to make another API request before it expires (5 minutes).
evidence.answer: The short-lived code expires after 5 minutes and must be exchanged, with client secret, client ID and redirect URI, for a token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Depending on the originating datacenter of the SurveyMonkey account, the API access URL may be different than https://api.surveymonkey.com .
evidence.answer: The API base URL can differ by the account's datacenter: EU and Canadian accounts use different hosts.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The API for the EU datacenter is https://api.eu.surveymonkey.com and the API for the Canadian datacenter is https://api.surveymonkey.ca .
evidence.answer: The EU datacenter API is api.eu.surveymonkey.com and the Canadian datacenter API is api.surveymonkey.ca.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The correct API access URL for each SurveyMonkey account is returned in the response body of the code for token exchange under the access_url key.
evidence.answer: The correct API access URL for each account is returned in the token-exchange response under the access_url key.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: To use our API, you’ll need to register a draft app to your SurveyMonkey account.
evidence.answer: To use the API, a draft app must be registered to the developer's SurveyMonkey account.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The client_secret can be found here .
evidence.answer: The client secret can be found at the link on the page (the page does not name the console location in plain words).

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The OAuth link should be https://api.surveymonkey.com/oauth/authorize with urlencoded parameters: redirect_uri , client_id , response_type and state .
evidence.answer: The authorization link is https://api.surveymonkey.com/oauth/authorize with redirect_uri, client_id, response_type and state parameters.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: response_type will always be set to the value code
evidence.answer: The response_type parameter must always be set to code.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_id the unique SurveyMonkey client id you got when registering your app
evidence.answer: The client ID is the unique client ID received when the app is registered.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Create a form-encoded HTTP POST request to https://api.surveymonkey.com/oauth/token with the following encoded form fields: client_id , client_secret , code , redirect_uri and grant_type .
evidence.answer: The token exchange is a form-encoded POST to /oauth/token with client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri and grant_type.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The grant type must be set to “authorization_code”.
evidence.answer: The grant_type for the token exchange must be authorization_code.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Obtain this token in the Settings of your app in the MY APPS tab.
evidence.answer: For a Private app, the access token is obtained in the Settings of the app under the MY APPS tab.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The value of the header must be “bearer” followed by a single space and then your access token.
evidence.answer: The access token is sent as an Authorization header in the form 'bearer' plus a single space and the token.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You can set scopes to be required, optional, or not required in your app’s settings .
evidence.answer: Scopes are set as required, optional, or not required in the app's settings.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps must adhere to SurveyMonkey's terms of use before publication (a use restriction; no user or install threshold is stated).

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Private apps are subject to our terms of use .
evidence.answer: Private apps are subject to SurveyMonkey's terms of use.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access .
evidence.answer: Private app users must all belong to the same SurveyMonkey team with a paid plan offering direct API access (eligibility rule).

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your email address needs to be verified in order to successfully send messages through our email invitation collector.
evidence.answer: The email address must be verified before sending messages through the email invitation collector.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The user’s email must be verified before performing this request.
evidence.answer: A user's email must be verified before certain requests can be performed.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Two scopes require SurveyMonkey's approval before use in a Public app (a use restriction).
